CaseSummary.description:
One queue row.

**Pseudonymous fields only, and no raw medical text** — that is a hard constraint from
`docs/canonical/03_architecture.md`, asserted by `test_queue_response_carries_no_medical_text`.
Narrative text appears only in the detail response, and then only the fragment a reason
depends on.

Field order mirrors the mandated column order: the sentence comes first.

reason_sentence.title: Reason Sentence

CaseSummary.title: CaseSummary

ClaimLineView.description:
One billed line with its support state.

`NOT_ASSESSABLE` is distinct from `UNSUPPORTED`: the first means the record was too thin
to judge, the second means the evidence is genuinely absent. Conflating them is the
difference between requesting a document and alleging a service never happened.
ClaimLineView.title: ClaimLineView

ComparisonCandidate.description: Side-by-side pair for repeat-billing and cloned-documentation reasons.

template_caveat.description: Present on clone reasons. Legitimate template-based documentation produces high similarity too, and the reviewer must read that before acting.
template_caveat.title: Template Caveat

ComparisonCandidate.title: ComparisonCandidate

CounterEvidenceDto.description:
One fact that argues against the reason it accompanies, **in words**.

The refs alone were shipped for a while and it hollowed the feature out: a reviewer saw
`Encounter ENC-PH-1` under a "counter-evidence" heading with nothing saying why it weakened
anything. The sentence is the argument; the references are only where to look next.

note.description: Working language, written by the rule that raised the reason.
note.title: Note

CounterEvidenceDto.title: CounterEvidenceDto

DispositionAction.description:
The four actions a human reviewer may take.

None of them is a verdict. `CONFIRM_ANOMALY` means the reviewer agrees an inconsistency
exists — it is not a finding of fraud, and the UI must say so before accepting it.
DispositionAction.title: DispositionAction

DispositionRequest.description:
A human decision. Never accepted without a reason.

`expected_case_version` is the optimistic lock. Overwriting a colleague's recorded
decision without knowing is an accountability failure, not a concurrency inconvenience —
so the version is required, not optional.

requested_evidence.description: For REQUEST_EVIDENCE: resource types being asked for. Editable by the reviewer.
requested_evidence.title: Requested Evidence

structured_reason.description: Chosen from the action's reason list.
structured_reason.title: Structured Reason

PriorityBand.description:
Queue ordering bands.

`NO_OBSERVED_RISK` means no selected detector fired at this engine version. It must never
be rendered as "clean" or "safe" — the system is not entitled to that claim.
PriorityBand.title: PriorityBand

QueueMetrics.description:
The five operational metrics above the queue. Exactly five.

Anything that does not change what a reviewer does next is excluded by
`docs/canonical/01_product_decision.md` § Main dashboard principles — no "fraud saved",
no provider league tables, no national projections.
QueueMetrics.title: QueueMetrics

ReasonCode.description: Stable identifiers used by the UI and by tests. Never renumbered.
ReasonCode.title: ReasonCode

ReasonDto.description:
One reason, with its evidence and whatever argues against it.

`counter_evidence` is a first-class field rather than a separate lookup: the reviewer must
see what weakens a signal on the same screen as the signal itself.

component_scores.description: Per-component scores, kept alongside the reason rather than collapsed.

RunManifest.description:
What makes a run reproducible.

Every field here is needed to rebuild the result from a clean environment and compare
hashes. A metric without its manifest cannot be defended when a judge asks how it was
produced.
RunManifest.title: RunManifest

ScreenRequest.description:
Screening carries no options.

There is deliberately no detector, threshold, or mode selection — the ingest screen offers
one button, and a configuration wizard would let a presenter tune their way to a result.

SourceAvailability.description:
Why a referenced resource can or cannot be shown in full.

Four outcomes, and keeping them apart is the whole point. Collapsing them into a boolean
would put a deliberate privacy boundary and a genuine integrity defect behind the same
empty panel, and `sprint/00-app-spec.md` § 4 rule 4 makes the second one a defect the
screen has to name.
SourceAvailability.title: SourceAvailability

SourceField.description: One field of a raw resource. Ordered pairs, so two renderings stay comparable.
SourceField.title: SourceField

SourceResource.description:
The resource behind an evidence reference, so every reference opens.

An unresolvable reference is recorded here with `MISSING` rather than dropped. Dropping it
would render as a shorter list — indistinguishable from a reason that cited less — which is
exactly how a broken evidence trail hides.
SourceResource.title: SourceResource

ToolCallRecord.description: One function the briefing chose to read. The log *is* the transparency artifact.
ToolCallRecord.title: ToolCallRecord

ValidationIssue.description:
One problem found in a submitted bundle, pointed at a specific resource.

`resource_type` and `resource_id` are what make the ingest screen's error list
actionable — the operator learns *which* resource to fix, not merely that something is
wrong somewhere.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation. Never contains medical text.
detail.title: Detail

ValidationIssue.title: ValidationIssue

ValidationStatus.description:
Three outcomes, not two.

`VALID_WITH_NOTES` exists because an incomplete record and a billed-but-unevidenced
service look identical at the schema level. Collapsing them into "valid" or "invalid" is
how this system would produce false accusations, so the distinction is in the type.
ValidationStatus.title: ValidationStatus

VersionStamp.description: Engine identity carried on every screening result and audit event.
VersionStamp.title: VersionStamp

info.description: Claim evidence integrity screening. Synthetic data only.
info.title: TilikKlaim API

get.description:
Does the briefing gateway answer, and does it hold the model that was configured?

Deliberately **not** part of `/healthz`: the platform probes that path, and a health check
that failed because an optional summariser was unreachable would restart the container over
a feature the product does not require.

Listing models tests the network and the credential at once without spending a token, and
`model_available: false` catches a mistyped model name before a reviewer's first click
rather than during a demo. The key is never in the response — `SecretStr` sees to that.

schema.title: Response Health Llm Health Llm Get

get.description: Liveness, the engine identity the runbook quotes, and demo readiness.

post.description: Validate a bundle and return counts, issues, and a deterministic input hash.
post.summary: Submit one synthetic bundle for validation

post.description:
Screen a validated bundle and return its reasons, band, and case.

Idempotent for the same input hash and engine version: re-screening returns the existing
case with its version bumped, rather than creating a second case for one claim.

get.description: The ordered work list. Pseudonymous fields only; no narrative text.
Claim lines, reasons with evidence and counter-evidence, timeline, and comparisons.
The full history. Restricted, because it names people and their decisions.

Observations with source references, open questions, and an uncertainty note.

Never a score, a band, or a state transition. Off by default; the deterministic template is
the answer when no model is configured.

post.description:
Record the reviewer's decision, or refuse and write nothing.

Nothing this endpoint does rejects a claim, releases or stops a payment, imposes a sanction,
or alters a code. It moves a case's state and appends an event, and that is the whole of it.

get.description: Read one run. The synthetic label travels with the payload, never as UI decoration.
